newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-CAMPBELL AND SAMUELS MAKE SOLID START.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CAMPBELL AND SAMUELS MAKE SOLID START.

text.p: West Indies openers Sherwin Campbell and Robert Samuels made a solid start in their pursuit of Australia's first innings 331 all out in the second test on Saturday.
The pair added 60 runs in 25 overs in an unbroken first-wicket partnership to lift the tourists' spirits after their bowlers laboured to dismiss Australia's lower order.
Campbell remained 27 not out alongside Samuels on 29 at tea on the second day at the Sydney Cricket Ground on a wicket that offered little menace or pace for the fast bowlers.
Earlier, Australia added 107 runs to their overnight total of 224 for five despite the setback of losing wicketkeeper Ian Healy for 44 to the second ball of the day.
Australia number 11 batsman Glenn McGrath typified Australia's stubborn resistance with a defiant innings of 24, easily his highest score in first-class cricket.

After adding 43 potentially crucial runs for the last wicket with fellow fast bowler Jason Gillespie, McGrath eventually fell leg before wicket to part-time spinner Jimmy Adams. McGrath previously averaged two with the bat in test cricket.
West Indies captain Courtney Walsh, who claimed five for 98 in 30 overs, was forced to rely on his makeshift spinner after his frontline bowlers failed to wrap up the innings.
Walsh added Healy, pace bowler Michael Kasprowicz and all-rounder Greg Blewett to his haul after removing top order pair Ricky Ponting and Mark Waugh on Friday.
It was the 12th time Walsh has taken five wickets in a test innings.
Blewett started the day on 58, added only 11 runs before deflecting the ball onto his thigh pad to give Adams a simple catch at short leg.
Australia won the first test in Brisbane by 123 runs on Tuesday.
